2352:
FEMALE GENITAL SYSTEM
The female genital (reproductive) system produces egg cells (oocytes) and the hormones oestrogen and progesterone, receives sperm, provides the site of fertilisation, and carries and nourishes a developing pregnancy.
The internal organs are the paired ovaries and uterine tubes, the uterus and the vagina, held in place in the lesser pelvis by peritoneal folds and ligaments. The external genitalia (vulva) surround the openings of the vagina and urethra. The breasts are accessory glands of the system.
### Blood supply
The ovarian arteries arise from the abdominal aorta; the uterine and vaginal arteries are branches of the internal iliac arteries. The two systems join along the side of the uterus.
### In this app
The 3D model comes from the Human Reference Atlas 3D Reference Object Library (Visible Human Female), CC BY 4.0, and has been scaled and placed into this body. Switch between the male and female body with the Male / Female control in the top bar.
2353:
FEMALE INTERNAL GENITALIA
The ovaries, uterine tubes, uterus and vagina lie in the lesser pelvis, between the urinary bladder in front and the rectum behind. The uterus normally tilts forward (anteverted) and bends forward on itself (anteflexed) so that it rests on the top of the bladder.
The 3D model comes from the Human Reference Atlas 3D Reference Object Library (Visible Human Female), CC BY 4.0, and has been scaled and placed into this body.
2354:
OVARY
The ovary is the female gonad: an almond-shaped organ about 3 cm long that produces oocytes and the sex hormones oestrogen and progesterone.
### Position
Each ovary lies against the side wall of the lesser pelvis in the ovarian fossa, attached to the back of the broad ligament by the mesovarium. The suspensory ligament of the ovary carries its vessels down from the pelvic brim; the ovarian ligament ties it to the uterus.
### Function
From puberty to menopause, each month a group of follicles matures under follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH); one releases its oocyte at ovulation, around day 14, triggered by a surge of luteinising hormone (LH). The empty follicle becomes the corpus luteum, which secretes progesterone to prepare the uterine lining.
### Blood supply and nerves
Ovarian artery from the abdominal aorta and the ovarian branch of the uterine artery. The ovarian veins drain to the inferior vena cava on the right and the left renal vein on the left. Lymph drains to the lumbar (para-aortic) nodes.
The 3D model comes from the Human Reference Atlas 3D Reference Object Library (Visible Human Female), CC BY 4.0, and has been scaled and placed into this body.
2355:
UTERINE TUBE
The uterine (fallopian) tube is a muscular tube about 10 cm long that runs from the ovary to the uterus in the upper border of the broad ligament. It catches the oocyte at ovulation, is the usual site of fertilisation, and moves the early embryo to the uterus over about four days.
### Parts
From lateral to medial: the infundibulum with its finger-like fimbriae around the abdominal opening, the wide ampulla (where fertilisation usually happens), the narrow isthmus, and the uterine (intramural) part that passes through the uterine wall.
### Clinical note
An embryo that implants in the tube (ectopic pregnancy) can rupture it, a surgical emergency.
The 3D model comes from the Human Reference Atlas 3D Reference Object Library (Visible Human Female), CC BY 4.0, and has been scaled and placed into this body.
2356:
INFUNDIBULUM OF UTERINE TUBE
The funnel-shaped lateral end of the uterine tube. It opens into the peritoneal cavity through the abdominal ostium and is fringed by the fimbriae, which sweep over the ovary to collect the oocyte at ovulation.
The 3D model comes from the Human Reference Atlas 3D Reference Object Library (Visible Human Female), CC BY 4.0, and has been scaled and placed into this body.
2357:
FIMBRIAE OF UTERINE TUBE
Finger-like projections around the abdominal opening of the uterine tube. At ovulation they move over the surface of the ovary and their cilia draw the oocyte into the tube. One longer fimbria (the ovarian fimbria) is attached to the ovary.
The 3D model comes from the Human Reference Atlas 3D Reference Object Library (Visible Human Female), CC BY 4.0, and has been scaled and placed into this body.
2358:
AMPULLA OF UTERINE TUBE
The widest and longest part of the uterine tube, between the infundibulum and the isthmus. Its folded lining makes it the usual site of fertilisation.
The 3D model comes from the Human Reference Atlas 3D Reference Object Library (Visible Human Female), CC BY 4.0, and has been scaled and placed into this body.
2359:
ISTHMUS OF UTERINE TUBE
The narrow, thick-walled medial third of the uterine tube, next to the uterus. It is the part that is cut or clipped in tubal sterilisation.
The 3D model comes from the Human Reference Atlas 3D Reference Object Library (Visible Human Female), CC BY 4.0, and has been scaled and placed into this body.
2360:
UTERINE PART OF UTERINE TUBE
The short intramural part of the uterine tube that passes through the wall of the uterus at the uterine horn and opens into the uterine cavity at the uterine ostium.
The 3D model comes from the Human Reference Atlas 3D Reference Object Library (Visible Human Female), CC BY 4.0, and has been scaled and placed into this body.
2361:
UTERUS
The uterus (womb) is a thick-walled, pear-shaped muscular organ about 7.5 cm long, 5 cm wide and 2.5 cm thick in a woman who has not been pregnant. It receives the embryo, holds and nourishes the fetus, and expels it at birth.
### Parts
The fundus is the rounded top above the openings of the uterine tubes; the body is the main part; the isthmus (lower uterine segment) is the narrow region above the cervix; the cervix projects into the vagina.
### Wall
The inner endometrium thickens and is shed each month in the menstrual cycle; the thick myometrium is smooth muscle that contracts in labour; the outer perimetrium is peritoneum.
### Position and support
Normally anteverted and anteflexed, resting on the bladder. It is supported mainly by the pelvic floor and by the cardinal, uterosacral and pubocervical ligaments; the round ligament helps keep it tilted forward.
### Blood supply
Uterine arteries from the internal iliac arteries, joining with the ovarian arteries. The uterine artery crosses above the ureter beside the cervix ("water under the bridge"), which matters in hysterectomy.
The 3D model comes from the Human Reference Atlas 3D Reference Object Library (Visible Human Female), CC BY 4.0, and has been scaled and placed into this body.
2362:
FUNDUS OF UTERUS
The rounded upper end of the uterus, above the level where the uterine tubes enter. Its height above the pubic symphysis is measured in pregnancy to follow the growth of the fetus.
The 3D model comes from the Human Reference Atlas 3D Reference Object Library (Visible Human Female), CC BY 4.0, and has been scaled and placed into this body.
2363:
BODY OF UTERUS
The main part of the uterus, between the fundus and the isthmus. It encloses the triangular uterine cavity, where the embryo implants into the endometrium.
The 3D model comes from the Human Reference Atlas 3D Reference Object Library (Visible Human Female), CC BY 4.0, and has been scaled and placed into this body.
2364:
UTERINE HORNS
The upper corners of the uterus (cornua) where the uterine tubes enter, on either side of the fundus. The round ligament and the ovarian ligament attach just below each horn.
The 3D model comes from the Human Reference Atlas 3D Reference Object Library (Visible Human Female), CC BY 4.0, and has been scaled and placed into this body.
2365:
ISTHMUS OF UTERUS
The narrow part of the uterus between the body and the cervix, about 1 cm long. In late pregnancy it stretches to form the lower uterine segment, where a caesarean incision is usually made.
The 3D model comes from the Human Reference Atlas 3D Reference Object Library (Visible Human Female), CC BY 4.0, and has been scaled and placed into this body.
2366:
CERVIX OF UTERUS
The lower, narrow, cylindrical part of the uterus, about 2.5 cm long. Its lower part projects into the vagina. Its canal runs from the internal os to the external os and is lined by mucus-secreting glands whose mucus changes during the cycle.
### Clinical note
The junction of its two linings (the transformation zone) is where cervical cancer usually starts; it is sampled in cervical screening.
The 3D model comes from the Human Reference Atlas 3D Reference Object Library (Visible Human Female), CC BY 4.0, and has been scaled and placed into this body.
2367:
INTERNAL OS OF UTERUS
The upper opening of the cervical canal, where the cervix joins the isthmus and the uterine cavity.
The 3D model comes from the Human Reference Atlas 3D Reference Object Library (Visible Human Female), CC BY 4.0, and has been scaled and placed into this body.
2368:
EXTERNAL OS OF UTERUS
The opening of the cervical canal into the vagina, at the tip of the cervix. It is small and round before childbirth and becomes a transverse slit after a vaginal birth. Dilation of the cervix in labour is measured here (0 to 10 cm).
The 3D model comes from the Human Reference Atlas 3D Reference Object Library (Visible Human Female), CC BY 4.0, and has been scaled and placed into this body.
2369:
VAGINA
The vagina is a muscular, distensible tube about 8 to 9 cm long that runs upward and backward from the vestibule of the vulva to the cervix. It is the birth canal, the passage for menstrual flow, and receives the penis in intercourse.
### Relations
In front: the bladder and urethra. Behind: the rectum and recto-uterine pouch. The cervix projects into its upper end, forming the vaginal fornices around it.
### Blood supply
Vaginal arteries and branches of the uterine and internal pudendal arteries.
The 3D model comes from the Human Reference Atlas 3D Reference Object Library (Visible Human Female), CC BY 4.0, and has been scaled and placed into this body.
2370:
VAGINAL FORNIX
The recess of the upper vagina around the projecting cervix, divided into anterior, posterior and lateral parts. The posterior fornix is the deepest and lies just below the recto-uterine pouch.
The 3D model comes from the Human Reference Atlas 3D Reference Object Library (Visible Human Female), CC BY 4.0, and has been scaled and placed into this body.
2371:
LIGAMENTS OF UTERUS AND OVARY
Peritoneal folds and bands of connective tissue that hold the uterus, uterine tubes and ovaries in position. The broad ligament with its parts (mesosalpinx, mesovarium, mesometrium) is a fold of peritoneum; the cardinal and uterosacral ligaments are condensations of pelvic fascia that give the main support to the cervix; the round and ovarian ligaments are remnants of the gubernaculum.
The 3D model comes from the Human Reference Atlas 3D Reference Object Library (Visible Human Female), CC BY 4.0, and has been scaled and placed into this body.
2372:
BROAD LIGAMENT OF UTERUS
A double fold of peritoneum that hangs over the uterus and uterine tubes like a sheet and extends to the side walls of the pelvis. It contains the uterine tube, the round and ovarian ligaments, and the uterine and ovarian vessels. Its parts are the mesosalpinx (beside the tube), the mesovarium (holding the ovary) and the mesometrium (beside the uterus).
The 3D model comes from the Human Reference Atlas 3D Reference Object Library (Visible Human Female), CC BY 4.0, and has been scaled and placed into this body.
2373:
MESOSALPINX
The part of the broad ligament that encloses the uterine tube, above the mesovarium. It carries the tubal branches of the uterine and ovarian vessels.
The 3D model comes from the Human Reference Atlas 3D Reference Object Library (Visible Human Female), CC BY 4.0, and has been scaled and placed into this body.
2374:
MESOVARIUM
The short fold of the broad ligament that attaches the front border (hilum) of the ovary to the back of the broad ligament. Vessels and nerves enter the ovary through it.
The 3D model comes from the Human Reference Atlas 3D Reference Object Library (Visible Human Female), CC BY 4.0, and has been scaled and placed into this body.
2375:
ROUND LIGAMENT OF UTERUS
A cord of fibrous tissue and smooth muscle from the uterine horn, through the deep inguinal ring and inguinal canal, to the labium majus. It helps keep the uterus anteverted. Stretching of it causes the "round ligament pain" common in pregnancy. It is the female remnant of the gubernaculum, matching part of the path of the male spermatic cord.
The 3D model comes from the Human Reference Atlas 3D Reference Object Library (Visible Human Female), CC BY 4.0, and has been scaled and placed into this body.
2376:
LIGAMENT OF OVARY
The ovarian ligament: a fibromuscular cord in the broad ligament that joins the lower pole of the ovary to the uterus, just below the uterine tube. Like the round ligament, it is a remnant of the gubernaculum.
The 3D model comes from the Human Reference Atlas 3D Reference Object Library (Visible Human Female), CC BY 4.0, and has been scaled and placed into this body.
2377:
SUSPENSORY LIGAMENT OF OVARY
A fold of peritoneum from the upper pole of the ovary to the side wall of the pelvis at the pelvic brim. It carries the ovarian artery, vein, lymph vessels and nerves, so it is also called the infundibulopelvic ligament.
The 3D model comes from the Human Reference Atlas 3D Reference Object Library (Visible Human Female), CC BY 4.0, and has been scaled and placed into this body.
2378:
CARDINAL LIGAMENT
The transverse cervical (Mackenrodt's) ligament: a condensation of pelvic fascia at the base of the broad ligament, from the cervix and upper vagina to the side wall of the pelvis. It is the main support of the uterus and carries the uterine vessels. Weakening of it contributes to uterine prolapse.
The 3D model comes from the Human Reference Atlas 3D Reference Object Library (Visible Human Female), CC BY 4.0, and has been scaled and placed into this body.
2379:
UTEROSACRAL LIGAMENT
A band of fibrous tissue and smooth muscle from the back of the cervix, around the rectum, to the front of the sacrum. It holds the cervix back and up, keeping the uterus anteverted, and supports the top of the vagina.
The 3D model comes from the Human Reference Atlas 3D Reference Object Library (Visible Human Female), CC BY 4.0, and has been scaled and placed into this body.
2380:
UTERINE ARTERY
A branch of the anterior division of the internal iliac artery. It runs medially in the base of the broad ligament, crosses above the ureter about 2 cm from the cervix, then climbs in a tortuous course along the side of the uterus and joins the ovarian artery. It supplies the uterus, the medial part of the uterine tube and the upper vagina, and enlarges greatly in pregnancy.
The 3D model comes from the Human Reference Atlas 3D Reference Object Library (Visible Human Female), CC BY 4.0, and has been scaled and placed into this body.
2381:
UTERINE VEIN
The uterine veins form a plexus beside the uterus and vagina in the broad ligament and drain to the internal iliac vein.
The 3D model comes from the Human Reference Atlas 3D Reference Object Library (Visible Human Female), CC BY 4.0, and has been scaled and placed into this body.
2382:
OVARIAN ARTERY
A branch of the abdominal aorta just below the renal arteries. It descends on the psoas muscle, crosses the ureter and the external iliac vessels at the pelvic brim, then passes in the suspensory ligament of the ovary and the broad ligament to the ovary and uterine tube, where it joins the uterine artery.
### In this app
The course above the pelvic brim is from the atlas (it matches the male testicular artery there). This part of the model is simplified: it was drawn for this app to show the course and connections, not traced from a scan.
2383:
OVARIAN VEIN
The ovarian veins leave the ovary as a plexus in the broad ligament and run up beside the ovarian artery. The right ovarian vein drains into the inferior vena cava and the left into the left renal vein, so left-sided problems (such as pelvic congestion) are more common.
### In this app
The course above the pelvic brim is from the atlas (it matches the male testicular vein there). This part of the model is simplified: it was drawn for this app to show the course and connections, not traced from a scan.
2384:
FEMALE URETHRA
The female urethra is about 4 cm long. It runs from the internal urethral orifice at the neck of the bladder down and forward, behind the pubic symphysis and in front of the vagina, to the external urethral orifice in the vestibule, just in front of the vaginal opening. It passes through the external urethral sphincter in the perineum.
### Clinical note
Because it is short and opens near the anus, urinary tract infections are much more common in women than in men.
### In this app
This part of the model is simplified: it was drawn for this app to show the course and connections, not traced from a scan.
2385:
BREAST
The breast (mamma) lies on the front of the chest wall, over the pectoralis major and serratus anterior, from about the 2nd to the 6th rib and from the sternum to the midaxillary line. An axillary tail extends up into the armpit. In women it contains the mammary gland, which produces milk after childbirth.
### Structure
15 to 20 lobes of glandular tissue, each draining by a lactiferous duct to the nipple, set in fat and divided by suspensory ligaments (Cooper's ligaments) that run from the skin to the deep fascia. The nipple is surrounded by the pigmented areola.
### Blood supply and lymph
Internal thoracic (mammary) artery, lateral thoracic and thoraco-acromial arteries, and intercostal arteries. About 75% of the lymph drains to the axillary nodes, the rest mostly to the parasternal nodes, which is why axillary nodes are checked in breast cancer.
### In this app
The 3D model comes from the Human Reference Atlas 3D Reference Object Library (Visible Human Female), CC BY 4.0, and has been scaled and placed into this body. The tissue was reshaped to sit on this body's chest wall.
2386:
ADIPOSE TISSUE OF BREAST
The fat of the breast, which surrounds the glandular lobes and gives the breast most of its size and shape. The amount varies widely between people and with weight, age and pregnancy.
The 3D model comes from the Human Reference Atlas 3D Reference Object Library (Visible Human Female), CC BY 4.0, and has been scaled and placed into this body.
2387:
SUSPENSORY LIGAMENTS OF BREAST
Cooper's ligaments: bands of connective tissue that run from the deep fascia over the pectoralis major through the breast to the skin, dividing and supporting the lobes. A cancer that pulls on them can cause dimpling of the skin.
The 3D model comes from the Human Reference Atlas 3D Reference Object Library (Visible Human Female), CC BY 4.0, and has been scaled and placed into this body.
2388:
LOBES OF MAMMARY GLAND
The mammary gland is made of 15 to 20 lobes arranged like the spokes of a wheel around the nipple. Each lobe is made of smaller lobules of milk-secreting alveoli, which enlarge in pregnancy and produce milk after birth under the influence of prolactin.
The 3D model comes from the Human Reference Atlas 3D Reference Object Library (Visible Human Female), CC BY 4.0, and has been scaled and placed into this body.
2389:
LACTIFEROUS DUCTS
One duct drains each lobe of the mammary gland and opens separately on the nipple. Oxytocin released during suckling contracts the cells around the alveoli and ducts to eject milk (the let-down reflex).
The 3D model comes from the Human Reference Atlas 3D Reference Object Library (Visible Human Female), CC BY 4.0, and has been scaled and placed into this body.
2390:
LACTIFEROUS SINUSES
The widened parts of the lactiferous ducts just beneath the areola, where milk collects before it is released at the nipple.
The 3D model comes from the Human Reference Atlas 3D Reference Object Library (Visible Human Female), CC BY 4.0, and has been scaled and placed into this body.
2391:
NIPPLE
The nipple (mammary papilla) projects from the centre of the areola, usually at the level of the 4th intercostal space in a young adult, though its position varies a lot in women. The lactiferous ducts open on its tip. It contains smooth muscle that makes it erect.
The 3D model comes from the Human Reference Atlas 3D Reference Object Library (Visible Human Female), CC BY 4.0, and has been scaled and placed into this body.
2392:
AREOLA
The circular area of pigmented skin around the nipple. It darkens in pregnancy. It contains areolar glands whose openings form small bumps (areolar tubercles).
The 3D model comes from the Human Reference Atlas 3D Reference Object Library (Visible Human Female), CC BY 4.0, and has been scaled and placed into this body.
2393:
AREOLAR TUBERCLES
Montgomery tubercles: small raised bumps on the areola made by the openings of areolar (sebaceous and rudimentary mammary) glands. Their secretion protects and lubricates the nipple during breastfeeding.
The 3D model comes from the Human Reference Atlas 3D Reference Object Library (Visible Human Female), CC BY 4.0, and has been scaled and placed into this body.
2394:
MAMMARY REGION
The region of the front of the chest over the breast, inside the pectoral region.
In the female body the skin surface here comes from the Visible Human Female and was reshaped onto this body's chest. The 3D model comes from the Human Reference Atlas 3D Reference Object Library (Visible Human Female), CC BY 4.0, and has been scaled and placed into this body.
2395:
UROGENITAL REGION
The front, triangular part of the perineum, between the pubic arch and a line joining the ischial tuberosities. In the female it contains the vulva: the mons pubis, the labia majora and minora, the clitoris, the vestibule with the openings of the urethra and vagina, and the greater vestibular glands.
### In this app
The female skin surface here comes from the Visible Human Female, fitted to this body's pelvis. Only the outer surface is modelled; the labia minora, clitoris and vestibular glands are not yet separate structures. The 3D model comes from the Human Reference Atlas 3D Reference Object Library (Visible Human Female), CC BY 4.0, and has been scaled and placed into this body.
